question_text: A 36-year-old woman comes to the physician to discuss contraceptive options. She is currently sexually active with one male partner, and they have not been using any contraception. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 15 years. She is allergic to latex and copper. A urine pregnancy test is negative. Which of the following contraceptive methods is contraindicated in this patient?

                    ### Question
                    A 36-year-old woman comes to the physician to discuss contraceptive options. She is currently sexually active with one male partner, and they have not been using any contraception. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 15 years. She is allergic to latex and copper. A urine pregnancy test is negative. Which of the following contraceptive methods is contraindicated in this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Diaphragm with spermicide
opb. Progestin-only pill
opc. Intrauterine device
opd. Condoms
ope. Combined oral contraceptive pill

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
For the 36-year-old woman who smokes and is allergic to latex and copper, the combined oral contraceptive pill is contraindicated due to the presence of estrogen, which can exacerbate cardiovascular risks in smokers. This is supported by the evidence path linking estrogens with oral contraceptives and their interaction with cardiovascular risks. Although she has allergies to latex and copper, non-latex condoms and non-copper intrauterine devices (IUDs) are available, making these options viable. The progestin-only pill is safe for smokers as it does not contain estrogen, and non-latex diaphragms are also a suitable option given her latex allergy. Therefore, the only contraindicated option in her case is the combined oral contraceptive pill.
